lesson_title: Scales and Street Maps: Reading Distance, Direction and Cost
hook_text: Photocopy a map and the scale printed on it turns into a lie. One thing on the page keeps telling the truth.
clip_script: The map says 1 to 25 000. Your route measures 8 centimetres. Multiply: 200 000 centimetres. Tidy up: 2 000 metres — 2 kilometres. That is the whole method: measure, multiply, tidy. Now shrink that map on a photocopier to fit your pocket. Every road just got smaller — but the printed ratio still says 1 to 25 000. It is lying now. Down in the corner, though, sits a little striped bar — and the bar shrank WITH the roads. Stripe for stripe, it still tells the truth on any copy, at any size. That is why real maps carry both. Now make the map pay for the trip. Road map, 1 to 200 000, route is 11 centimetres — 22 kilometres. At 55 an hour: 22 divided by 55 is 0,4 hours. Not 40 minutes — 0,4 times 60 is 24 minutes. The car sips 7,5 litres per 100 k's, so 1,65 litres, R37,62 each way. Minibus wants R60 return. Alone? Take the minibus. Four of you? The car's R75,24 beats the minibus's R240 by more than R164. The map just paid for lunch.
visual_style: A street map of Mbombela under a moving ruler; the map sliding through a photocopier and shrinking while the printed ratio flashes red and the bar scale glows green; the route unrolling into kilometres, minutes and a petrol pump display.
mood: Practical and road-trip ready, the confidence of a navigator who has never been lost.
pacing: Measured through the three-step method, a sharp gotcha at the photocopier, brisk acceleration through the time-fuel-money chain.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn any map into distances, minutes and rands.
